user: A weekly GitHub repo tracker now lives at the repo root — deploy it next to your Railway Postgres to start building stars/forks/issues time series every Sunday.
what: Added the GitHub Repo Tracker app: a weekly Railway Cron service that upserts GitHub repos and metric snapshots (stars, forks, open issues, watchers, size) into the project's Postgres over internal networking, plus wiki pages documenting the app and the Railway cron/private-networking pattern.
why: The project needs durable numerical tracking of GitHub repos over time; this gives it a cheap, idempotent pipeline (one runtime dep, minutes of compute per week) with zero manual schema management.

user: Wiki now explains exactly which GitHub endpoints the tracker uses (and why /user/repos isn't one of them), so nobody reintroduces the wrong repo source later
what: Added two learnings to the knowledge wiki: the difference between GitHub's /user/repos, /users/{owner}/repos, and /search/repositories endpoints (what the tracker uses today, the 1,000-result search cap, and what switching to private repos would entail), and a workflow gotcha that failed edit batches apply nothing rather than partially. Also repaired two broken wiki links on the GitHub Repo Tracker entity page.
why: The endpoint distinction came up as a direct user question and the answer (public-owner + search only; private repos need a repo-scoped token and break the contributor-count stat) isn't obvious from the code alone — documenting it prevents a future session from wiring /user/repos in without understanding the consequences.
next: See docs/wiki/learnings/github-repo-list-endpoint-semantics-user-repos-vs-users-owne.md before touching any repo-listing API call
summary: Recorded two learnings: (1) GitHub repo-list endpoint semantics — /user/repos (token-accessible, may include private) vs /users/{owner}/repos (public, used by GITHUB_OWNERS) vs /search/repositories (1,000/query cap, used by GITHUB_SEARCH_QUERIES), plus private-repo knock-on effects for the contributors-based collaborator stat and the undecided GITHUB_SOURCE_SELF option; (2) edit batches are atomic — a failed edit means nothing in that batch landed. Also fixed two broken relative links in the GitHub Repo Tracker entity page (scope decision + Railway networking pattern).
